abstract: The pandemic wheat blast fungus Magnaporthe oryzae destroys wheat but cannot infect rice, a form of resistance so uniform that it does not segregate in genetic crosses and cannot be mapped. We broke this nonhost resistance into single-gene phenotypes by expressing individual effectors from the wheat-infecting pathotype, one at a time, in a rice-infecting isolate. Screening 35 effectors across 20 rice cultivars (700 combinations) identified six that trigger resistance. One, eTO5, is recognized by Pi-eTO5, a genetically linked quartet of NLR immune receptors: SQ1, SQ2, and SQ4 are required for resistance, whereas SQ3 prevents constitutive defense activation dependent on the other three. eTO5 is conserved across the pandemic B71 lineage spanning South America, Asia and Africa. Effector transfer into a compatible pathogen should make nonhost resistance genetically tractable in other host-pathogen systems.
